references.properties: Clot stiffness in 0.5-2 kPa range; tested human stroke clot samples

references.author: Fereidoonnezhad et al. (2017)

references.journal: Journal of the Mechanical Behavior of Biomedical Materials
references.properties: Used continuum damage mechanics with hyperelastic-damage model; porcine blood clots; uniaxial tension tests; Ogden-type SED with damage variables
references.relevance: DIRECTLY relevant — uses CDM for clot fracture. Their damage parameters need to be compared to our (alpha, beta) domain.

domain_mapping.question: Do published clot damage parameters fall within our validity domain (alpha [0.002, 0.500], beta [0.010, 0.095])?
domain_mapping.analysis: Fereidoonnezhad et al. (2017) is the most relevant — they used CDM for clot fracture. Their damage model parameters need to be mapped to our Simo CDF (alpha, beta) formulation. This requires reading the actual paper (per Rule 6: primary evidence required).
domain_mapping.preliminary_assessment: Blood clots are SOFT biological tissues (E ~ 0.5-2 kPa for acute stroke clots, higher for chronic). Their damage behavior depends on composition (RBC-rich vs fibrin-rich). RBC-rich clots are softer and more fragile (lower alpha, lower beta → more likely in our domain). Fibrin-rich clots are stiffer and tougher (higher alpha, higher beta → may be outside domain).
domain_mapping.key_insight: The validity domain (beta < 0.1) corresponds to materials with VERY LOW residual strength — i.e., BRITTLE materials that lose almost all strength when damaged. Blood clots, especially RBC-rich acute stroke clots, ARE brittle (they fragment during retrieval). This is consistent with our domain.
domain_mapping.risk: Fibrin-rich clots may have beta > 0.1 (tougher, more residual strength) and would be OUTSIDE our domain. The invention claim must specify that it applies to BRITTLE clot types (RBC-rich), not all clots.
domain_mapping.per_rule_9: SEARCH_INCOMPLETE — need to read Fereidoonnezhad et al. (2017) for actual parameter values

conclusion.preliminary: Based on OX Alpha knowledge (MODEL_DERIVED, per Rule 6), blood clots — particularly RBC-rich acute stroke clots — are likely BRITTLE with low residual strength (beta < 0.1), placing them WITHIN our validity domain. However, fibrin-rich clots may be tougher (beta > 0.1) and OUTSIDE the domain.
conclusion.next_step: Read Fereidoonnezhad et al. (2017) for actual damage parameter values. Map their parameters to our Simo CDF (alpha, beta) formulation.
conclusion.bounded_claim_revision: The invention claim should be revised to specify: 'For BRITTLE clot types (beta < 0.1, typically RBC-rich acute stroke clots), the dD/dstrain deceleration predicts fragmentation.' This is a more honest, clinically-relevant bound.
conclusion.per_article_I: Claim bounded to clot types where the signal is valid

honest_caveats.rule_6: OX Alpha knowledge is MODEL_DERIVED. Need primary literature (actual papers).
honest_caveats.rule_9: SEARCH_INCOMPLETE — specific clot damage parameters not yet verified.
honest_caveats.article_I: Claim must be bounded to clot types where parameters fall in validity domain.
honest_caveats.article_XXIX: If fibrin-rich clots have beta > 0.1, the signal won't work for them — this is a domain limitation, not a mechanism failure.
